Counts the bits of a number that are 1. This is a BlitzLLVM extension. It looks at the bits of the number the way its type has them, so the same value counts differently as a `Byte`, an `Int` or a `Long`: a number written in the program is an `Int` (32 bits) unless it is larger, and `Byte`, `UByte`, `Short`, `UShort`, `UInt`, `Long` and `ULong` give the other widths. A real or a text is taken as an `Int`, like the bit operators do.

```blitzbasic
;run
Print PopCount(255)
Print PopCount(-1)
Print PopCount(Byte(-1))
Print PopCount(ULong(-1))
```

```text
8
32
8
64
```
@param value  An integer.
@returns How many bits are 1.
@gap Not in the originals.
